title: Perro to dog, dog to perro
hook: You always get 'perro → dog' right. Does it work the other way round?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that recall works in the direction you practise, so testing word-to-meaning does not check meaning-to-word

misconception: If you can give a word's meaning, you can also produce the word from its meaning.
objective: Distinguish two directions of an arbitrary word-pair mapping.

claims.text: Stage: the card (dax → red, wug → blue, zib → green) shows at the prediction and is covered after it (? → ?, ? → ?, ? → ?). Each answer box starts empty and cycles through fixed choices (zib: green, red, blue; dax: red, blue, green; wug: blue, green, red; red: dux, dax, zib; blue: wug, wog, dax; green: zeb, zib, wug). Pressing each box once gives: Word → meaning 3 of 3; Meaning → word 1 of 3. Reveal sentences: Both directions passed this time, but only testing each one could show it.

recall.question: You can say 'dog' when you see 'perro'. Which check tests the other direction?
recall.why: Swapping cue and answer tests the opposite mapping; success in one direction is not a test of the other.
